description: CLOVER is a Python model developed for community-scale energy planning and rural electrification. It combines device-use profiles, solar generation, storage, diesel generation and grid-availability assumptions to simulate or optimize an energy system. Users supply CSV and YAML inputs describing a location, its equipment, use patterns and financial or greenhouse-gas assumptions. The documented workflow uses hourly profiles, with the geographical setting and simulation bounds chosen for each community. Source, a Python distribution and an example location are publicly available free under MIT. The model supports comparisons of minigrid capacity, reliability and economic choices. A limitation is that suitable local demand and equipment assumptions are still needed, and automatically fetching solar profiles requires a Renewables.ninja account and API key. Existing data-renewables-ninja is the documented solar-profile service. The code was not installed, profiles were not requested, and the public example was not treated as evidence that any proposed system was built or operated.
